contentFull:
Voltrac moves Thor robot into pre-series production

 07-09 | Field robots | News

LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

The Thor runs on hot-swappable battery packs that deliver up to 20 hours of uninterrupted operation. Photo: Voltrac

Spanish agtech startup Voltrac has confirmed that its Thor autonomous electric robot is moving into pre-series production. The company’s current Thor 2 model – recently demonstrated at a robotics event in Berlin – is described by its founders as a pre-serial vehicle, with the follow-up Thor 3 set to be the first production-ready version.

Voltrac plans to manufacture 96 units per year at its 1,200-square-metre factory in Valencia as a first phase, with longer-term blueprints targeting 1,000 vehicles per year. The Thor is not a converted diesel tractor with an electric motor dropped in. Voltrac built it from the ground up with autonomy as the starting point – and that distinction shapes nearly every engineering decision the company has made.

No more leaks and failures

A conventional tractor carries a gearbox, oil filters, radiators, and a range of components that are prone to leaks and failures. Voltrac eliminated all of them. ‘By just removing them and electrifying, all we have is cables, instead of complex mechanisms’, company co-founder Francisco Infante Aguirre points out. The result is a machine with roughly 70 percent fewer components than a traditional tractor.

In place of a conventional drivetrain, Voltrac uses one electric motor per wheel – four in total – each paired with a reduction box. That configuration delivers 20,000 Newton metres of wheel torque. Four-wheel propulsion also means tight turning circles, which is relevant for orchard and vineyard work where headland space is limited and maximising planted rows directly increases yield.

If one motor fails, the other three carry on. ‘It’s a tool. It’s a workhorse. It has to carry on pushing’, according to Infante Aguirre. Repairs are designed to be done on-farm: each motor unit is accessible with two bolts, and Voltrac ships replacement units directly to the customer.

Battery and power

The Thor runs on hot-swappable battery packs that deliver up to 20 hours of uninterrupted operation. Rather than charging in the field, operators can carry a second set of packs and swap them out in minutes. Voltrac is also partnering with solar panel manufacturers to give customers a complete off-grid energy solution for charging.

Hydraulics are currently retained for implement compatibility, but Voltrac expects to phase them out as implements increasingly switch to electric power – eliminating fluid leaks on the field entirely.

One of the Thor’s central selling points for existing farm operations is its three-point hitch, which makes it compatible with any implement a farmer already owns. ‘For farmers, they don’t have to buy anything fancy or new’, Infante Aguirre explains.

The robot carries a dual compute module – one for functional safety, and one running a CPU-GPU combination for machine learning – along with stereo cameras front and rear and mono cameras on the sides. Every pass over a field can be used to monitor crop health, detect disease early, and optimise fertiliser and chemical inputs. The platform is also open to third parties: Voltrac allows external developers to run their own applications on the robot’s compute, effectively creating a marketplace for field-level tools.

Connectivity runs through dual SIM cards and a Starlink connection, with a remote teleoperator always available.

One operator supervising multiple vehicles

The key operational model is one operator supervising multiple vehicles across multiple fields simultaneously — rather than one person per machine. GPS precision sits at around 5 centimetres.

Voltrac produces the Thor in Valencia. Infante Aguirre: ‘The talent is here, the precision manufacturing is here. The know-how is here.’ With Thor 3 and serial production now the immediate target, Voltrac is moving from demonstration to delivery.

translationZh:
西班牙农业科技初创公司Voltrac已确认，其Thor自主电动机器人正在进入预量产阶段。该公司目前的Thor 2型号——最近在柏林的一场机器人活动上进行了演示——被其创始人描述为一款预量产车辆，后续的Thor 3将成为首个量产版本。

Voltrac计划在其位于瓦伦西亚的1200平方米工厂中，作为第一阶段每年生产96台，长期蓝图目标为每年1000台。Thor并不是将柴油拖拉机改装后塞入电动机的产品。Voltrac从零开始构建它，以自主性为起点——这一区别塑造了该公司几乎每一个工程决策。

**不再有泄漏和故障**

传统拖拉机带有变速箱、机油滤清器、散热器以及一系列容易泄漏和故障的部件。Voltrac将它们全部消除。公司联合创始人Francisco Infante Aguirre指出：“仅仅通过移除它们并电气化，我们拥有的只是电缆，而不是复杂的机械结构。”结果是，这台机器的部件数量比传统拖拉机减少了约70%。

Voltrac没有采用传统传动系统，而是每个车轮使用一个电动机——总共四个——每个都配有一个减速箱。这种配置可提供20000牛顿米的轮端扭矩。四轮驱动还意味着更小的转弯半径，这对于果园和葡萄园作业非常重要，因为这些地方地头空间有限，而最大化种植行数直接增加产量。

如果一个电机发生故障，另外三个可以继续工作。Infante Aguirre表示：“它是一个工具。它是一匹干活的马。它必须继续前进。”维修被设计为可在农场内完成：每个电机单元只需两个螺栓即可拆卸，Voltrac直接将替换单元运送给客户。

**电池与动力**

Thor采用热插拔电池组，可提供长达20小时的不间断运行。操作人员无需在田间充电，而是可以携带第二套电池组，在几分钟内完成更换。Voltrac还与太阳能电池板制造商合作，为客户提供完整的离网能源充电解决方案。

目前保留了液压系统以兼容农具，但Voltrac预计随着农具越来越多地转向电力驱动，液压系统将逐步淘汰——从而完全消除田间的液体泄漏。

Thor对现有农场运营的核心卖点之一是其三点悬挂，这使其与农民已经拥有的任何农具兼容。Infante Aguirre解释说：“对农民来说，他们不必购买任何花哨或新的东西。”

该机器人搭载双计算模块——一个用于功能安全，另一个运行CPU-GPU组合用于机器学习——以及前后立体相机和两侧单目相机。每次在田间作业都可以用于监测作物健康、早期发现病害并优化肥料和化学品投入。该平台也对第三方开放：Voltrac允许外部开发者在该机器人的计算平台上运行自己的应用程序，实际上创建了一个田间级工具的市场。

连接通过双SIM卡和Starlink连接实现，远程操作员始终可用。

**一名操作员监管多台车辆**

关键的运营模式是一名操作员同时监管多个田间的多台车辆——而不是每台机器配一个人。GPS精度约为5厘米。

Voltrac在瓦伦西亚生产Thor。Infante Aguirre表示：“人才在这里，精密制造在这里。专业知识在这里。”随着Thor 3和批量生产成为当前目标，Voltrac正从演示走向交付。
